blocks.notes: Cooling and heating states hold for ten minutes. Warm AHU supply caps cooling flow at the active minimum; heating raises flow only after discharge is 3 K above zone temperature.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

blocks.name: cool_deadband
blocks.notes: Cooling starts only after the room exceeds its setpoint by 0.5 °C.

blocks.name: zero
blocks.notes: Shared zero signal for disabled reheat and the heating-mode comparison.

blocks.name: minimum_damper
blocks.notes: Keeps the damper at least 15% open for ventilation.

blocks.name: minimum_airflow
blocks.notes: Base airflow estimate before pressure and damper effects are added.

blocks.name: cool_error
blocks.notes: Positive when the room is warmer than the cooling setpoint.

blocks.name: heat_error
blocks.notes: Positive when the room is colder than the heating setpoint.

blocks.name: cooling_mode
blocks.notes: Checks whether cooling error exceeds the 0.5 °C deadband.

blocks.name: heating_mode
blocks.notes: Enables reheat only when room temperature is below the heating setpoint.

blocks.name: cool_pi
blocks.notes: PI loop turns room temperature error into a damper increment, capped at 85%.

blocks.name: heat_pi
blocks.notes: Reverse-acting PI loop turns low room temperature into a reheat command.

blocks.name: damper_offset
blocks.notes: Adds the minimum ventilation position to the cooling PI command.

blocks.name: damper_limit
blocks.notes: Clamps the requested damper position to 15–100%.

blocks.name: damper_select
blocks.notes: Uses the cooling damper request when cooling is enabled; otherwise holds minimum ventilation.

blocks.name: reheat_select
blocks.notes: Passes the heating PI command only in heating mode; otherwise closes reheat.

blocks.name: flow_span
blocks.notes: Scales the damper command into the variable part of the airflow estimate.

blocks.name: pressure_effect
blocks.notes: Reduces estimated flow when duct pressure is low.

blocks.name: airflow_sum
blocks.notes: Adds minimum airflow to the pressure-adjusted variable flow.

blocks.name: airflow_request_sum
blocks.notes: Adds minimum airflow to the damper request before pressure effects; this demand drives the AHU fan.

blocks.name: cool_demand_gain
blocks.notes: Converts positive cooling error into a normalized plant request.

blocks.name: heat_demand_gain
blocks.notes: Converts positive heating error into a normalized plant request.

blocks.name: cool_demand_limit
blocks.notes: Keeps zone cooling demand between zero and one.

blocks.name: heat_demand_limit
blocks.notes: Keeps zone heating demand between zero and one.

blocks.name: maximum_discharge_temp
blocks.notes: Editable terminal discharge temperature upper target; physical coil safety remains at 40 °C.

blocks.name: discharge_headroom
blocks.notes: Temperature rise allowed above measured AHU supply air.

blocks.name: reheat_capacity_per_flow
blocks.notes: Converts temperature headroom to valve capacity: 1.2 kW per airflow-K divided by the 8 kW reheat coil.

blocks.name: reheat_flow_cap
blocks.notes: Scale valve cap by measured primary airflow.

blocks.name: reheat_cap_limit
blocks.notes: Keep the discharge-temperature-derived valve cap between closed and open.

blocks.name: reheat_capped
blocks.notes: Limit zone heating command with the discharge temperature cap.

blocks.name: low_flow_fraction
blocks.notes: Alarm when measured flow stays below half of its request.

blocks.name: low_flow_threshold
blocks.notes: Half of requested primary airflow.

blocks.name: low_flow_detected
blocks.notes: Measured primary airflow is below half the request.

blocks.name: flow_alarm_enable_threshold
blocks.notes: OBC 0.05 m³/s near-zero flow guard; one teaching airflow unit equals 1 m³/s.

blocks.name: flow_requested
blocks.notes: Only monitor low flow while the box requests air.

blocks.name: low_flow_condition
blocks.notes: Request exists and delivered primary flow is low.

blocks.name: low_flow_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes of newly deficient primary flow; an already deficient input at initialization alarms immediately, as in OBC TrueDelay.

blocks.name: high_discharge_detected
blocks.notes: Measured discharge temperature exceeds the editable upper target.

blocks.name: high_discharge_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes above the discharge upper target before alarm.

blocks.name: high_discharge_alarm_priority
blocks.notes: Teaching priority for persistent high discharge: 3 while active, 0 when clear. This level is not yet reference-verified.

blocks.name: standby_cool
blocks.notes: Occupied standby cooling setpoint after five minutes vacant.

blocks.name: standby_heat
blocks.notes: Occupied standby heating setpoint after five minutes vacant.

blocks.name: unoccupied_cool
blocks.notes: G36 unoccupied cooling setback setpoint.

blocks.name: unoccupied_heat
blocks.notes: Editable unoccupied heating setback; the three-hour optimal-start cap can recover from this teaching target.

blocks.name: standby_damper
blocks.notes: No occupied-standby ventilation minimum while the zone is vacant.

blocks.name: unoccupied_damper
blocks.notes: No ventilation minimum outside occupied schedule.

blocks.name: standby_airflow
blocks.notes: No occupied-standby airflow minimum while the zone is vacant.

blocks.name: unoccupied_airflow
blocks.notes: No minimum airflow outside occupied schedule.

blocks.name: presence_delay
blocks.notes: Require one continuous minute of presence before setting occupied.

blocks.name: presence_inverse
blocks.notes: True when the raw occupancy sensor reports vacant.

blocks.name: vacancy_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes vacant before clearing occupied.

blocks.name: occupancy_latch
blocks.notes: Hold confirmed occupancy until the vacancy delay clears it.

blocks.name: conditioning_mode
blocks.notes: Request occupied temperature setpoints during the schedule or the preconditioning window.

blocks.name: cool_setpoint_standby
blocks.notes: Select occupied or sensor-vacant standby value.

blocks.name: cool_setpoint_active
blocks.notes: Select scheduled or unoccupied value.

blocks.name: heat_setpoint_standby
blocks.notes: Select occupied or sensor-vacant standby value.

blocks.name: heat_setpoint_active
blocks.notes: Select scheduled or unoccupied value.

blocks.name: minimum_damper_standby
blocks.notes: Select occupied or sensor-vacant standby value.

blocks.name: minimum_damper_active
blocks.notes: Select scheduled or unoccupied value.

blocks.name: minimum_airflow_standby
blocks.notes: Select occupied or sensor-vacant standby value.

blocks.name: minimum_airflow_active
blocks.notes: Select scheduled or unoccupied value.

blocks.name: minimum_damper_heating
blocks.notes: Preserve minimum discharge airflow during a heating call.

blocks.name: minimum_airflow_heating
blocks.notes: Preserve minimum discharge airflow during a heating call.

blocks.name: heating_damper_gain
blocks.notes: Increase primary-air damper opening as the heating PI demand rises.

blocks.name: heating_damper_offset
blocks.notes: Add heating demand to the zone's active minimum damper position.

blocks.name: heating_damper_limit
blocks.notes: Keep heating damper command within its physical travel.

blocks.name: heating_damper_select
blocks.notes: Use the heating airflow path during a heating call; otherwise retain the cooling/ventilation path.

blocks.name: discharge_max_rise
blocks.notes: Maximum heating discharge target above the active zone heating setpoint.

blocks.name: discharge_upper
blocks.notes: Active heating setpoint plus the editable maximum rise.

blocks.name: discharge_span
blocks.notes: Difference from AHU supply target to maximum heating discharge target.

blocks.name: discharge_zero_rise
blocks.notes: Do not request a negative reheat span.

blocks.name: discharge_positive_span
blocks.notes: Nonnegative discharge temperature rise available for heating.

blocks.name: discharge_demand_double
blocks.notes: Reach maximum discharge target at 50% heating-loop demand.

blocks.name: discharge_demand_limit
blocks.notes: Keep discharge reset fraction between zero and one.

blocks.name: discharge_reset_rise
blocks.notes: Scale available temperature rise by heating-loop demand.

blocks.name: discharge_reset_target
blocks.notes: Reset target from AHU supply temperature to active heating setpoint plus 11 K.

blocks.name: discharge_target_cap
blocks.notes: Apply the editable absolute discharge temperature upper bound.

blocks.name: discharge_minimum
blocks.notes: Minimum discharge temperature for the low-temperature reheat exception.

blocks.name: discharge_target
blocks.notes: Use heating reset target in heating mode; otherwise protect the 10 °C minimum.

blocks.name: discharge_valve_pi
blocks.notes: Reset the reheat PI to a closed valve on each heating or low-discharge enable; gain is tuned to the simplified 8 kW coil.

blocks.name: discharge_below_minimum
blocks.notes: OBC minimum-discharge threshold: assert below the editable minimum and clear 0.25 K above it.

blocks.name: discharge_minimum_occupied
blocks.notes: Apply the 10 °C minimum-discharge exception only in occupied mode.

blocks.name: discharge_valve_enable
blocks.notes: Enable reheat during a heating call or occupied low-discharge protection.

blocks.name: discharge_valve_closed
blocks.notes: Close reheat valve outside heating and low-temperature protection.

blocks.name: discharge_valve_select
blocks.notes: Gate the discharge-temperature PI valve command.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_midpoint
blocks.notes: The first half of heating demand resets discharge temperature, not airflow.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_excess
blocks.notes: Heating demand above the 50% discharge-reset stage.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_double
blocks.notes: Map the upper half of heating demand to the full heating airflow range.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_limit
blocks.notes: Keep the upper-stage heating airflow fraction in its valid range.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_margin
blocks.notes: Only increase heating flow when discharge exceeds room temperature by 3 K.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_threshold
blocks.notes: Room temperature plus the editable warm-discharge margin.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_warm
blocks.notes: Measured discharge air is warm enough to increase primary flow.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_enabled
blocks.notes: Only raise airflow in heating mode with warm discharge air.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_zero
blocks.notes: Hold heating airflow at its active minimum until the warm-discharge condition is met.

blocks.name: heating_airflow_select
blocks.notes: Apply the upper-stage heating airflow request only after discharge is warm.

blocks.name: heating_warmup_full
blocks.notes: Use the heating airflow maximum during preconditioning warm-up.

blocks.name: heating_warmup_airflow
blocks.notes: In preconditioning, use the heating maximum instead of the occupied-stage airflow request.

blocks.name: damper_flow_pi
blocks.notes: OBC-style PI tracks primary airflow and resets to 1% damper output when AHU fan proof rises.

blocks.name: damper_flow_threshold
blocks.notes: Close the damper when the airflow setpoint is effectively zero.

blocks.name: damper_flow_requested
blocks.notes: The terminal has a nonzero primary-airflow setpoint.

blocks.name: damper_closed
blocks.notes: Command a closed damper when primary airflow is not requested.

blocks.name: damper_feedback_output
blocks.notes: Use the measured-airflow PI command only while primary air is requested.

blocks.name: measured_airflow_passthrough
blocks.notes: Expose measured primary airflow separately from its commanded setpoint.

blocks.name: ventilation_occupied
blocks.notes: Ventilation applies only when the schedule and confirmed occupancy are both active.

blocks.name: ventilation_window_eligible
blocks.notes: An open window suppresses mechanical ventilation components for this zone.

blocks.name: ventilation_floor_area
blocks.notes: Synthetic design floor area served by this zone, in square metres.

blocks.name: ventilation_area_rate
blocks.notes: Editable ASHRAE 62.1 breathing-air design rate per square metre.

blocks.name: ventilation_area_design
blocks.notes: Design floor area times outdoor-air rate per area.

blocks.name: ventilation_person_rate
blocks.notes: Editable ASHRAE 62.1 breathing-air design rate per person.

blocks.name: ventilation_population_design
blocks.notes: Measured occupant count times outdoor-air rate per person.

blocks.name: ventilation_zero
blocks.notes: No breathing-zone air in unoccupied or standby mode.

blocks.name: ventilation_area_active
blocks.notes: Gate the area component by occupied presence.

blocks.name: ventilation_population_active
blocks.notes: Gate the population component by occupied presence.

blocks.name: ventilation_breathing_sum
blocks.notes: Sum the area and population components.

blocks.name: ventilation_cooling_supply
blocks.notes: Measured room air warmer than discharge air selects cooling distribution effectiveness with OBC hysteresis.

blocks.name: ventilation_cooling_effectiveness
blocks.notes: Cooling air-distribution effectiveness.

blocks.name: ventilation_heating_effectiveness
blocks.notes: Heating air-distribution effectiveness.

blocks.name: ventilation_effectiveness
blocks.notes: Select heating or cooling distribution effectiveness.

blocks.name: ventilation_minimum_oa
blocks.notes: Breathing-zone outdoor air divided by distribution effectiveness.

blocks.name: co2_reset_lower
blocks.notes: Start increasing occupied minimum airflow 200 ppm below the CO₂ setpoint.

blocks.name: co2_reset_span
blocks.notes: Editable CO₂ proportional reset span.

blocks.name: co2_above_lower
blocks.notes: Measured CO₂ above the reset start.

blocks.name: co2_reset_ratio
blocks.notes: Normalize the CO₂ error by the editable span.

blocks.name: co2_reset_limit
blocks.notes: Match the OBC CO₂ reset line from setpoint minus 200 ppm to setpoint.

blocks.name: co2_cooling_max_flow
blocks.notes: Teaching design cooling maximum for this VAV.

blocks.name: co2_available_flow
blocks.notes: Cooling maximum minus the current occupied minimum.

blocks.name: co2_flow_increment
blocks.notes: Scale available flow by CO₂ reset fraction.

blocks.name: co2_flow_reset
blocks.notes: Raise occupied minimum airflow toward cooling maximum.

blocks.name: co2_population_component
blocks.notes: Reset the measured-count population ventilation component from zero to design as CO₂ rises.

blocks.name: co2_minimum_flow
blocks.notes: Apply the CO₂ reset only with scheduled, confirmed occupancy.

blocks.name: window_primary_minimum
blocks.notes: Suppress the occupied primary-air minimum when the window contact is open; freeze heating remains a separate request.

blocks.name: warmup_error
blocks.notes: Occupied heating target minus measured room temperature.

blocks.name: cooldown_error
blocks.notes: Measured room temperature minus occupied cooling target.

blocks.name: setback_error
blocks.notes: Unoccupied heating target minus measured room temperature.

blocks.name: setup_error
blocks.notes: Measured room temperature minus unoccupied cooling target.

blocks.name: warmup_needed
blocks.notes: Editable temperature deadband prevents mode chatter near the target.

blocks.name: cooldown_needed
blocks.notes: Editable temperature deadband prevents mode chatter near the target.

blocks.name: setback_needed
blocks.notes: Editable temperature deadband prevents mode chatter near the target.

blocks.name: setup_needed
blocks.notes: Editable temperature deadband prevents mode chatter near the target.

blocks.name: warmup_mode
blocks.notes: Warm-up only inside the schedule lookahead window.

blocks.name: cooldown_mode
blocks.notes: Cooldown only inside the schedule lookahead window.

blocks.name: preconditioning_needed
blocks.notes: Restore occupied targets only when warm-up or cooldown is needed.

blocks.name: occupied_setpoint_requested
blocks.notes: Use occupied setpoints for confirmed presence or thermal preconditioning.

blocks.name: mode_unoccupied
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for unoccupied.

blocks.name: mode_occupied
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for occupied.

blocks.name: mode_standby
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for standby.

blocks.name: mode_warmup
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for warmup.

blocks.name: mode_cooldown
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for cooldown.

blocks.name: mode_setup
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for setup.

blocks.name: mode_setback
blocks.notes: Local teaching mode code for setback.

blocks.name: mode_select_setback
blocks.notes: Choose the setback mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: mode_select_setup
blocks.notes: Choose the setup mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: mode_select_cooldown
blocks.notes: Choose the cooldown mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: mode_select_warmup
blocks.notes: Choose the warmup mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: mode_select_occupied
blocks.notes: Choose the occupied mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: mode_select_schedule
blocks.notes: Choose the schedule mode from CDL conditions.

blocks.name: damper_is_unoccupied
blocks.notes: Identify local unoccupied mode before commanding the damper fully closed.

blocks.name: damper_operation_enabled
blocks.notes: Allow the measured-airflow PI to respond to a zero-flow override outside unoccupied mode.

blocks.name: unoccupied_heat_off
blocks.notes: Disable ordinary unoccupied heating outside group setback/freeze.

blocks.name: unoccupied_cool_off
blocks.notes: Disable ordinary unoccupied cooling outside group setup.

blocks.name: group_heat_allowed
blocks.notes: Permit unoccupied heat during group setback or freeze protection.

blocks.name: unoccupied_heat_enabled
blocks.notes: Select group setback target or off target.

blocks.name: unoccupied_cool_enabled
blocks.notes: Select group setup target or off target.

blocks.name: mode_freeze_setback
blocks.notes: Local teaching code 7 for group zone-freeze setback.

blocks.name: mode_select_freeze_setback
blocks.notes: Show group freeze setback before ordinary setback/setup.

blocks.name: window_heat_permit
blocks.notes: Freeze setback keeps heating available with a window open.

blocks.name: window_heat_target
blocks.notes: Disable ordinary heating while the window is open.

blocks.name: window_cool_target
blocks.notes: Disable cooling while the window is open.

blocks.name: local_occupied
blocks.notes: Scheduled occupancy or local override selects occupied zone control.

blocks.name: low_flow_fan_ready
blocks.notes: A fan newly proven on qualifies after 30 continuous minutes; an already-on fan at initialization qualifies immediately, following OBC TrueDelay.

blocks.name: low_flow_occupied_and_fan
blocks.notes: Only an occupied zone with proven AHU fan operation may raise a low-flow alarm.

blocks.name: low_flow_seventy_setpoint
blocks.notes: Level 3 fault threshold is 70% of the active primary-airflow setpoint.

blocks.name: low_flow_below_seventy
blocks.notes: Measured primary airflow is below 70% of setpoint.

blocks.name: low_flow_eligible
blocks.notes: Allow the moderate alarm only for an occupied zone with a nonzero airflow request.

blocks.name: low_flow_occupied_gate
blocks.notes: Apply occupied and pressure-importance eligibility after the severe flow timer.

blocks.name: low_flow_seventy_condition
blocks.notes: Fan-proven measured flow is below the Level 3 threshold.

blocks.name: low_flow_seventy_output_gate
blocks.notes: Apply occupied, request, and importance eligibility after the moderate flow timer.

blocks.name: low_flow_severe_request_gate
blocks.notes: Apply the separately timed nonzero-request gate after the severe flow timer.

blocks.name: low_flow_request_delay
blocks.notes: OBC waits five minutes after a newly nonzero airflow setpoint; an already nonzero setpoint qualifies at initialization.

blocks.name: low_flow_seventy_delay
blocks.notes: OBC TrueDelay alarms immediately when already below 70% at initialization; later deficits persist five minutes.

blocks.name: low_flow_alarm_zero
blocks.notes: No terminal low-airflow alarm.

blocks.name: low_flow_alarm_three
blocks.notes: Level 3 sustained low-airflow alarm.

blocks.name: low_flow_alarm_two
blocks.notes: Level 2 severe low-airflow alarm.

blocks.name: low_flow_alarm_moderate
blocks.notes: Show Level 3 after the 70% fault delay.

blocks.name: low_flow_alarm_priority
blocks.notes: Severe Level 2 fault takes precedence over Level 3.

blocks.name: high_discharge_eligible
blocks.notes: Only diagnose high discharge temperature while the zone is locally occupied and the AHU fan is proven.

blocks.name: high_discharge_condition
blocks.notes: Start the high-discharge timer only with valid fan and occupied proof.

blocks.name: pressure_importance
blocks.notes: Zero removes this zone from duct-pressure reset and suppresses its low-airflow alarm.

blocks.name: pressure_importance_zero
blocks.notes: Disabled-importance threshold.

blocks.name: pressure_importance_positive
blocks.notes: Only a positive pressure-reset importance enables requests and the related low-flow alarm.

blocks.name: pressure_damper_hysteresis
blocks.notes: OBC's shared damper latch starts above 95% and clears at or below 85%; it qualifies every request tier.

blocks.name: pressure_damper_sample
blocks.notes: Sample damper command at the same 120-second period as AHU pressure trim and respond.

blocks.name: pressure_setpoint_sample
blocks.notes: Sample active primary-airflow setpoint with the damper command.

blocks.name: pressure_measured_sample
blocks.notes: Sample measured primary airflow for the same pressure-request instant.

blocks.name: pressure_damper_delay
blocks.notes: OBC waits one minute after the sampled damper request, independently of changing airflow.

blocks.name: pressure_setpoint_positive
blocks.notes: OBC permits high-tier requests only when sampled setpoint exceeds 0.01, clearing below 0.005.

blocks.name: pressure_flow_half
blocks.notes: Severe request threshold is 50% of active airflow setpoint.

blocks.name: pressure_flow_seventy
blocks.notes: Moderate request threshold is 70% of active airflow setpoint.

blocks.name: pressure_below_half
blocks.notes: Measured primary airflow is below 50% of setpoint with 0.01 flow hysteresis.

blocks.name: pressure_below_seventy
blocks.notes: Measured primary airflow is below 70% of setpoint with 0.01 flow hysteresis.

blocks.name: pressure_damper_flow_eligible
blocks.notes: The sampled damper has requested pressure for one minute and airflow setpoint is positive.

blocks.name: pressure_severe_eligible
blocks.notes: The severe flow deficit has a nonzero setpoint.

blocks.name: pressure_moderate_eligible
blocks.notes: The moderate flow deficit has a nonzero setpoint.

blocks.name: pressure_level_0
blocks.notes: 0 duct-pressure reset requests.

blocks.name: pressure_level_1
blocks.notes: 1 duct-pressure reset requests.

blocks.name: pressure_level_2
blocks.notes: 2 duct-pressure reset requests.

blocks.name: pressure_level_3
blocks.notes: 3 duct-pressure reset requests.

blocks.name: pressure_one_request
blocks.notes: Send one request while the damper hysteresis is active.

blocks.name: pressure_two_requests
blocks.notes: Two requests take precedence after a sustained 70% flow deficit.

blocks.name: pressure_three_requests
blocks.notes: Three requests take precedence after a sustained 50% flow deficit.

blocks.name: pressure_importance_select
blocks.notes: A zero importance suppresses all pressure requests.

blocks.name: low_flow_importance_gate
blocks.notes: A zero pressure-reset importance suppresses both low-airflow alarm levels.

blocks.name: sat_cooling_error
blocks.notes: Zone temperature minus active cooling setpoint.

blocks.name: sat_two_error_high
blocks.notes: Cooling error exceeds 2 K, clearing below 1.75 K.

blocks.name: sat_three_error_high
blocks.notes: Cooling error exceeds 3 K, clearing below 2.75 K.

blocks.name: sat_two_error_delay
blocks.notes: Two continuous minutes above the hysteretic 2 K threshold.

blocks.name: sat_three_error_delay
blocks.notes: Two continuous minutes above the hysteretic 3 K threshold.

blocks.name: sat_cooling_loop_high
blocks.notes: One request starts above 95% of the cooling PI loop and holds until below 85%.

blocks.name: sat_cooling_loop_scale
blocks.notes: Normalize the existing cooling PI's 0–0.85 damper command to a 0–1 cooling-loop signal. Retune this gain if the PI output maximum changes.

blocks.name: sat_cooling_loop_limit
blocks.notes: Keep the normalized cooling loop within the OBC 0–1 input range.

blocks.name: sat_previous_cooling_setpoint
blocks.notes: Sample the active cooling setpoint every two minutes for change suppression.

blocks.name: sat_sampled_cooling_setpoint
blocks.notes: Sample the active cooling target every two minutes before detecting a material setpoint change, matching the OBC TimeSuppression input sampler.

blocks.name: sat_setpoint_rise
blocks.notes: Current setpoint minus previous sample.

blocks.name: sat_setpoint_fall
blocks.notes: Previous setpoint minus current sample.

blocks.name: sat_change_threshold
blocks.notes: Ignore setpoint changes of 0.25 K or less.

blocks.name: sat_setpoint_rise_detected
blocks.notes: Detect a material setpoint rise.

blocks.name: sat_setpoint_fall_detected
blocks.notes: Detect a material setpoint fall.

blocks.name: sat_setpoint_changed
blocks.notes: Either setpoint direction starts suppression.

blocks.name: sat_two_eligible
blocks.notes: Two requests require sustained error and completed suppression.

blocks.name: sat_three_eligible
blocks.notes: Three requests require sustained error and completed suppression.

blocks.name: sat_level_0
blocks.notes: 0 cooling supply-air temperature reset requests.

blocks.name: sat_level_1
blocks.notes: 1 cooling supply-air temperature reset requests.

blocks.name: sat_level_2
blocks.notes: 2 cooling supply-air temperature reset requests.

blocks.name: sat_level_3
blocks.notes: 3 cooling supply-air temperature reset requests.

blocks.name: sat_request_one
blocks.notes: One request while the cooling-loop proxy is high.

blocks.name: sat_request_two
blocks.notes: Two sustained-error requests take precedence.

blocks.name: sat_request_three
blocks.notes: Three sustained-error requests take precedence.

blocks.name: sat_startup_true
blocks.notes: Begin the first-sampling-period guard at initialization.

blocks.name: sat_startup_delay
blocks.notes: Ignore setpoint changes during the first 120 seconds, as in OBC TimeSuppression.

blocks.name: sat_change_after_startup
blocks.notes: Only a sampled setpoint change after startup resets suppression.

blocks.name: sat_change_latch
blocks.notes: Hold the first material setpoint change until its suppression interval expires.

blocks.name: sat_clear_to_real
blocks.notes: Carry the passed flag through a sampled state break.

blocks.name: sat_clear_previous
blocks.notes: Clear the suppression latch at the next 120-second sample.

blocks.name: sat_clear_boolean
blocks.notes: Convert the delayed passed flag back to Boolean.

blocks.name: sat_latch_inactive
blocks.notes: Requests are eligible whenever no setpoint-change interval is active.

blocks.name: sat_change_edge
blocks.notes: Capture the next material setpoint change once.

blocks.name: sat_change_setpoint
blocks.notes: setpoint at the setpoint change.

blocks.name: sat_change_room_temp
blocks.notes: room_temp at the setpoint change.

blocks.name: sat_change_error
blocks.notes: Setpoint minus room temperature when the change occurred.

blocks.name: sat_change_error_reverse
blocks.notes: Room temperature minus setpoint when the change occurred.

blocks.name: sat_change_error_abs
blocks.notes: Magnitude of the zone error when the setpoint changes.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_rate
blocks.notes: OBC request suppression: 540 seconds per Kelvin of zone error.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_maximum
blocks.notes: Cap request suppression at 30 minutes.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_duration
blocks.notes: Minimum of 540 s/K times captured zone error and 1800 seconds.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_timer
blocks.notes: Elapsed time while the first setpoint change remains latched.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_passed
blocks.notes: Release after elapsed time exceeds the calculated duration.

blocks.name: sat_suppression_complete
blocks.notes: Allow requests outside a latched change or once its suppression time has passed.

blocks.name: sensor_fan_off
blocks.notes: Diagnose the flow sensor only while the AHU fan motor is proven off.

blocks.name: sensor_fan_off_delay
blocks.notes: Require ten continuous minutes of fan-off proof before checking residual flow.

blocks.name: sensor_cooling_design_flow
blocks.notes: Editable design cooling maximum: 0.2 minimum plus 0.75 cooling span in this example.

blocks.name: sensor_ten_percent
blocks.notes: A reading above ten percent of design cooling flow indicates sensor calibration trouble while the fan is off.

blocks.name: sensor_residual_flow
blocks.notes: Measured primary flow exceeds ten percent of design cooling flow.

blocks.name: sensor_alarm_condition
blocks.notes: Fan proven off for ten minutes and measured flow remains above the design threshold.

blocks.name: sensor_alarm_zero
blocks.notes: No airflow sensor calibration alarm.

blocks.name: sensor_alarm_three
blocks.notes: Level 3 airflow sensor calibration alarm.

blocks.name: sensor_alarm_select
blocks.notes: Publish Level 3 only when the fan-off residual-flow condition is true.

blocks.name: low_discharge_importance
blocks.notes: Set to zero to suppress this zone's hot-water reset alarms.

blocks.name: low_discharge_zero_importance
blocks.notes: Alarm suppression threshold.

blocks.name: low_discharge_important
blocks.notes: Hot-water reset importance must be positive to allow alarms.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Editable floor area and breathing-air rates combine with measured occupant count. Occupied presence gates area and population ventilation; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. Measured CO₂ resets occupied minimum primary airflow through editable CDL; the physical model only supplies concentration. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. High-discharge temperature diagnosis requires local occupied mode and AHU fan proof throughout its five-minute delay. Duct-pressure reset samples damper, setpoint, and measured flow together every 120 seconds; one minute of damper request qualifies the 2/3 levels. A zero importance suppresses requests and low-airflow alarms. Cooling SAT reset sends editable 0–3 requests from zone error and the normalized cooling PI loop; higher tiers wait through setpoint-change suppression. SAT request suppression now follows the editable 540 s/K captured-error calculation, capped at 1800 s. Pinned OBC SystemRequests hot-water tiers issue 3/2 after five minutes more than 17/8 K below the discharge target, or 1 while the reheat valve is above 95% (clear below 85%). A separate plant request holds until the valve falls below 10%. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Low-discharge error timers run on measured temperature; occupied mode, physical fan and heating-source proof, and editable reset importance gate the published Level 3/2 alarms. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise. An editable occupied-standby policy retains area ventilation and base primary minimum during vacancy where standby is disallowed; population air still follows confirmed presence. OBC integer airflow override codes 1–4 select zero, nominal cooling maximum, design minimum, or nominal heating maximum before damper feedback. Normal primary airflow setpoint follows editable OBC cooling, deadband, and heating mapping independently of damper command.

blocks.name: zone_group_1
blocks.description: Five-zone CDL operating-mode coordinator for one AHU.
blocks.notes: Each closed-window zone samples its error at the start horizon. A CDL latch opens a recovery episode only after optimal start is requested, then holds observation into occupied operation. CDL samples the held recovery rate at midnight when the sampled horizon error calls for optimal start, and learns a three-day slope from measured setpoint attainment within fourteen hours, and uses the longest zone prediction. The editable seconds-per-kelvin constants initialize and bound the learned slopes. A sampled prior rate explicitly breaks the group feedback loop. Full G36 group mode coordination and reference-trace verification remain to be added. Each zone now uses the editable OBC ZoneStatus temperature hysteresis, window-gated recovery time, and setback/setup status. Former duplicate comparators and window gates have been removed. The OBC OperationMode composite supplies the mode requests. Editable CDL priority switches select one mode when the reference block requests simultaneous modes; integer counts and thresholds remain editable. Pinned OBC GroupStatus now supplies occupied status, group recovery extrema, cold/hot/open counts, setback/setup triggers, and zone temperature extrema to OperationMode. Each zone's warm-up and cooldown time now comes from the pinned OBC OptimalStartCalculation CDL graph. The group mode and window filter remain editable CDL decisions.

blocks.name: zone_group_2
blocks.description: Five-zone CDL operating-mode coordinator for one AHU.
blocks.notes: Each closed-window zone samples its error at the start horizon. A CDL latch opens a recovery episode only after optimal start is requested, then holds observation into occupied operation. CDL samples the held recovery rate at midnight when the sampled horizon error calls for optimal start, and learns a three-day slope from measured setpoint attainment within fourteen hours, and uses the longest zone prediction. The editable seconds-per-kelvin constants initialize and bound the learned slopes. A sampled prior rate explicitly breaks the group feedback loop. Full G36 group mode coordination and reference-trace verification remain to be added. Each zone now uses the editable OBC ZoneStatus temperature hysteresis, window-gated recovery time, and setback/setup status. Former duplicate comparators and window gates have been removed. The OBC OperationMode composite supplies the mode requests. Editable CDL priority switches select one mode when the reference block requests simultaneous modes; integer counts and thresholds remain editable. Pinned OBC GroupStatus now supplies occupied status, group recovery extrema, cold/hot/open counts, setback/setup triggers, and zone temperature extrema to OperationMode. Each zone's warm-up and cooldown time now comes from the pinned OBC OptimalStartCalculation CDL graph. The group mode and window filter remain editable CDL decisions.

notes: Compare this sample with FourPipeBuildingControls using the same weather, equipment, and physical model. Each zone has a debounced Brick occupancy sensor. Occupied setpoints are 21/24 °C, standby widens them by 0.5 K, and unoccupied setback/setup targets are 18/32 °C. Ventilation minimums and AHU fan minimums also reset. Qualified VAV cooling requests drive a sampled AHU supply-air temperature reset. Two five-zone CDL group controllers coordinate optimal start within three hours of occupancy, shared unoccupied setback/setup, and a zone freeze setback alarm. The AHUs use outdoor/return temperature comparisons and measured mixed-air feedback to modulate free cooling. Measured primary airflow and discharge temperature feed an editable terminal discharge setpoint and valve loop, plus editable measured-feedback terminal alarms. Timed Stage 1–3 AHU freeze protection overrides air delivery and requests water-side pumps; Stage 2 interrupts outdoor ventilation for one hour after a deeper fault, while Stage 3 latches shutdown. This is a G36-inspired subset; full G36 economizer limits, plant staging, alarms, and CO₂ sequence validation remain. Two five-zone CDL group controllers coordinate warm-up and cooldown using a three-hour cap and sampled VAV occupied setpoints. Two five-zone CDL group controllers now command latched setback, setup, and zone freeze setback. Raw window contacts feed editable CDL group exclusion and terminal conditioning gates. Local override button contacts feed editable two-hour CDL holds before zone/group occupancy and Level 4 window alarms. CDL per-zone recovery learners replace fixed-rate optimal-start predictions; Rust supplies only schedule time and measured zone temperatures. VAV low-airflow alarms are calculated from measured delivery in editable CDL. Duct-pressure reset receives 0–3 zone requests from editable CDL rather than a binary teaching shortcut. Cooling SAT request levels and setpoint-change suppression are calculated in each editable VAV composite. Fan-off airflow sensor calibration alarms are editable CDL and use physical motor status and flow feedback. VAV low-discharge alarms are calculated in editable CDL from measured temperatures and physical hot-water source-operation proof. Physical VAV actuator positions and seat-leak behavior feed editable CDL terminal leakage alarms. Physical fan status remains a raw input; editable CDL decides fan discrepancy alarms. Supply fan drive speed feedback is physical; its tracking alarm is CDL. AHU intake physics uses measured damper positions; CDL diagnoses command mismatch. Economizer high-limit state holds are editable CDL, with separate immediate fan and freeze gates. Each AHU has an editable fixed versus differential dry-bulb high-limit choice. Economizer combined dry-bulb high limits are editable CDL choices. The sample does not impose the former teaching low-temperature economizer cutoff by default. Economizer enable does not require a separate cooling-demand condition by default. Economizer disable damper transitions follow editable CDL timers. VAV alarm acknowledgements are tracked by editable CDL latches from raw per-zone operator button contacts. AHU alarm acknowledgements are independent editable CDL latches driven by raw operator contacts. Plant source and water-pump fault acknowledgements are independent editable CDL latches driven by a raw operator contact.
